notes.1a: Many candidates knew that the organisms belonged to the arthropod group.
notes.1bi: The vast majority of candidates were awarded both marks for using the diagram to describe two features of Musca .
notes.2ai: Photosynthesis was correctly stated by most candidates. A few candidates stated respiration.
notes.2aii: Very few candidates knew that magnesium is required to make chlorophyll. Incorrect answers included water, iron and sodium.
notes.2aiii: Many candidates could state that chlorophyll is found in chloroplasts. Incorrect answers included cell, cytoplasm, leaf and cell membrane.
notes.2bi: This was well-answered with most identifying structure B . A few candidates wrote A which was the upper epidermis and cuticle.
notes.2bii: Cuticle was often given, whilst it does not contain chlorophyll, it is not a tissue. Lower epidermis was also incorrect as the guard cells contain chlorophyll.
notes.3ai: Many candidates were awarded two marks. Some candidates put the xylem vessels and mesophyll cells the wrong way round.
notes.3aii: Few candidates were awarded full marks. Many responses were too vague, such as transpiration is the movement of water through the plant , with no mention of evaporation from the mesophyll cells, diffusion through the stomata or loss of water vapour.
notes.3aiii: Most candidates were able to correctly state that water was used for photosynthesis, but few were able to state another use, such as support, transport or solvent.
notes.3b: Most candidates correctly stated that the pot of damp soil was placed in the plastic bag to reduce water loss from the soil. Very few recognised that this was done to ensure that the readings taken only measured the water loss from the leaves.
notes.3ci: Most candidates were able to accurately extract the required information from the graph and were awarded three marks.
notes.3cii: This proved challenging with few candidates gaining all the available marks. Candidates often stated that water loss increased as temperature increased but did not qualify this by saying this was only the case in the first three hours.
notes.4ai: Most candidates were able to identify the two parts of the CNS. Several candidates stated spine rather than spinal cord and could not be awarded the mark.
notes.4aii: Few candidates were able to give the function of the nervous system as coordination or regulation of body functions. Most answers were in terms of sensitivity or ability to respond to a stimulus, which are descriptions of parts of the nervous system rather than its function as a whole.
notes.4bi: Many candidates did not identify the structures as neurones despite the fact that this was given in the question.
notes.4bii: Few candidates could correctly give a feature of a reflex action.
notes.4biii: Most candidates could give an example of a reflex action. This was usually the withdrawal response.
notes.4ci: Few candidates were awarded marks as answers were often too vague. It was not widely known that heroin is a depressant.
notes.4cii: Most candidates could give examples of the long-term effects of excessive alcohol consumption. Common correct answers included liver damage and addiction.
notes.5a: Definitions of ingestion and egestion were well-known. Many candidates identified the definition of assimilation as absorption, perhaps not fully reading the definition given.
notes.5bi: Anaerobic respiration was well-known by many candidates.
notes.5bii: Most candidates gave the correct answer.
notes.5biii: Many candidates realised that oxygen must be stopped from entering the jar when alcohol is being made.
notes.5biv: Almost all candidates knew that enzymes break down glucose molecules.
notes.6ai: Some candidates did not read the question carefully and gave the names of the parts rather than their functions.
notes.6aii: Many candidates could identify the sepal and the ovary. Often, stamen was given instead of filament.
notes.6bi: Some candidates gave correct responses but many found this challenging. The male flowers are exposed so the pollen can be blown by the wind. The female flowers are lower down so they can catch pollen drifting downwards.
notes.6bii: Many candidates described differences between wind-pollinated and insect-pollinated flowers rather than differences between the pollen. When answering comparative questions, it is essential that candidates make comparative statements such as heavier or lighter.
notes.7a: Few candidates made any mention of energy and therefore gave incomplete definitions. A herbivore is an organism that gets its energy from eating plants and a carnivore is an organism that gets its energy from eating other animals, or consumers.
notes.7bi: Generally very well-answered. A few candidates got 2 and 3 the wrong way round.
notes.7bii: Many candidates were unfamiliar with pyramids of numbers and found this question demanding. Successful candidates shaded 21 boxes on row 2 and 7 boxes on row 3 and then labelled the rows as herbivore and carnivore.
notes.8ai: The effects of deforestation were well-known.
notes.8aii: Many candidates did not read the question carefully and referred to the effects on the monoculture rather than the effects on the ecosystem. Loss of habitats was the most commonly awarded mark.
notes.8b: Generally, this question was well-answered, with most candidates describing at least one way of conserving endangered species.
notes.9ai: The question asked for two parts of a balanced diet that were missing from the label. Some candidates did not read the question carefully and gave two different vitamins or minerals. Other incorrect answers included sugar, calories, fruit, vegetables, grains, and dairy.
notes.9aii: The majority of candidates correctly stated mammals.
notes.9bi: Generally this was answered well with many candidates scoring two or three marks for describing the dietary importance of fats, carbohydrates and proteins.
notes.9bii: This question proved demanding. Few candidates realised that nitrogen is found in proteins but not in fats or carbohydrates. Common incorrect answers included amino acids, calcium, oxygen, fibre, and hydrogen.
notes.9c: Some candidates gave answers in terms of preventing CHD, others included aspects of diet despite these being excluded by the question. This again highlights the importance of reading the question carefully.
notes.10ai: Many candidates found this challenging and few successfully used the term alleles in their answer.
notes.10aii: Almost all candidates correctly stated that all offspring had red flowers despite one of the parents having white flowers.
notes.10b: Many candidates found this question very demanding. Candidates should be encouraged to practise questions of this type and work through each stage methodically.
